navigation.title: SEF Carbon and Air Quality Explorer

meta.description: Base layer: OpenStreetMap
Base layer: Sentinel-2 cloudless mosaic 2024
Base layer: Terrain Light by EOX

Column-mean CO2 (XCO2) in ppm from the CAMS global greenhouse gas forecast, which assimilates satellite CO2 observations. **Latest 3-hourly forecast step**, **global** on a **9 km** model grid.

How to read: values sit near 420 ppm everywhere, and emission regions show as enhancements of a few ppm. Switch on a NO2 layer to locate combustion sources. This is a live forecast, so the map changes from one forecast step to the next.

Column-mean methane (XCH4) in ppb from the CAMS global greenhouse gas forecast, which assimilates satellite observations. **Latest 3-hourly forecast step**, **global** on a **9 km** model grid.

How to read: look for regional enhancements over oil and gas basins, coal regions and wetlands. This is a live forecast, so the map changes from one forecast step to the next.

Column-averaged CO2 (XCO2) in ppm measured directly along the OCO-2 track, for **one day, 17 August 2025**. The track is **about 10 km wide** and each sounding about 1.3 by 2.3 km.

How to read: zoom in to see the strips. Each strip is one orbit; gaps are cloud or places the satellite did not pass over that day, and coverage builds up over successive days. Compare with the CAMS CO2 column, which fills the gaps with a model.

sources.name: Carbon dioxide anomaly against the global mean (OCO-2)

meta.description:
OCO-2 XCO2 minus the global mean, in ppm, for **one day, 17 August 2025**, along the same **10 km wide track** as the OCO-2 total column.

How to read: positive values lie above the global mean, usually over emitting regions; negative values where vegetation takes up carbon. Read the pattern along a strip rather than single soundings.

Column-averaged methane (XCH4) in ppb, **mean of 2025**, from Sentinel-5P TROPOMI processed by S5P-PAL. **Global**, pixels **5.5 by 7 km**. The colour scale is stretched to 1,880 to 1,980 ppb to separate regional sources.

How to read: persistent hotspots stand out over coal, oil and gas regions and wetlands. Open Data Values and click the map for the value in a cell.

Tropospheric NO2 column in µmol/m², **mean of 2025**, from Sentinel-5P TROPOMI processed by S5P-PAL. **Global**, pixels **5.5 by 3.5 km**. The colour scale is stretched to 25 to 95 µmol/m² so large plants stand out from the rural background.

How to read: NO2 stays close to its source, so the map traces power plants, industry, cities and shipping lanes. Values are for the whole air column, not the air at ground level. Lower the opacity slider to see place names underneath. Open Data Values and click the map for the value in a cell.

NOx emission rates in kg/s for **1,139 point sources worldwide**, **2021**. Estimated from Sentinel-5P NO2 and ERA5 winds with the flux divergence method, on a 0.025 degree grid (about 2.5 km).

How to read: larger dots are larger emitters. Click a dot and open Data Values for the rate and its error. Switch on the power plants layer to see which sources are power stations. The estimates agree with UBA and US EPA reports within 20% on average.

attribution.text: ESA World Emission, NOx point source catalogue

meta.description:
Fossil and waste-fired power plants, coloured by main fuel: coal, gas, oil and waste. **Global**, from the Global Power Plant Database **v1.3 (2021)**.

How to read: click a plant and open Data Values for its name, country, fuel and capacity. Fuel and capacity are as recorded in the database. Combine with the NOx point sources to see which emitters are power plants.

Gas, crude oil and NGL pipelines across **Europe, Türkiye and the Caucasus**, about 1,080 pipelines and segments, coloured by fuel. Thinner lines are under construction, proposed or idle. From the Global Energy Monitor trackers (**gas November 2025, oil June 2026**).

How to read: click a line and open Data Values for owner, capacity, diameter, length, start year and a link to its GEM wiki page. Use it as context for methane sources along the main transport corridors.

Steelworks where CO2 plumes have been detected from space: **18 plants in Asia, Türkiye and Italy**, detections **from 2022 to 2026** by the hyperspectral satellites EnMAP, PRISMA, EMIT and Tanager. Larger dots mean more detections.

How to read: visible at any zoom. Click a site and open Data Values for the number of detections, the satellites and the first and latest dates. Then zoom in on the site and switch on the plume footprints, or the Taranto and Ereğli plume layers, to see the plumes themselves.

Footprints of single CO2 plumes at steel plants, one shape per detection, **2022 to 2026**, from imagery at **30 to 60 m**. Emission rates are in tonnes of CO2 per hour (t/h).

How to read: the shapes are about 1 km across, so they only appear when zoomed in on a plant; use the steelworks site layer to find them. Click a plume and open Data Values for the emission rate, its uncertainty, the satellite and the detection time. Each shape is one clear-sky overpass, so compare detections with each other rather than reading one as a yearly figure.

The CO2 plume over the Taranto steelworks as the satellite saw it: the enhancement of the CO2 column above background (ΔXCO2) in ppm, in **30 to 60 m pixels**. **6 detections, 30 April 2025 to 11 April 2026**, by EMIT, EnMAP and Tanager.

How to read: use the zoom button in this panel to fly to the plant, then the time control to step from one detection to the next. Brighter colours mean more CO2 above background. Click a pixel and open Data Values for its ΔXCO2 and the emission rate of that detection in t/h.

The CO2 plume over the Erdemir steelworks in Ereğli as the satellite saw it: the enhancement of the CO2 column above background (ΔXCO2) in ppm, in **30 m pixels**. **3 detections, 24 July 2025 to 27 April 2026**, all by EnMAP.

How to read: use the zoom button in this panel to fly to the plant, then the time control to step from one detection to the next. Brighter colours mean more CO2 above background. Click a pixel and open Data Values for its ΔXCO2 and the emission rate of that detection in t/h.

NOx emitted by ships in kg per grid cell per year, **annual, 2019 to 2023**, over **European seas** (15°W to 40°E, 25°N to 74°N) on a **5 km** grid. Computed ship by ship by the FMI STEAM model from AIS positions, engine data and the weather, for the ESA EO4SEM project.

How to read: use the time control to step through the years. Shipping lanes and ports stand out. Lower the opacity slider to see place names underneath. Open Data Values and click the map for the value in a cell.
meta.units: kg NOx per cell per year

attribution.text: FMI STEAM model, ESA EO4SEM project

meta.description:
NOx emitted from cropland in kg of nitrogen per hectare per year, estimated from Sentinel-5P NO2 by inverse modelling (KNMI DECSO). **Monthly, January to December 2025**, each month expressed as an annual rate, over **Europe** on a **0.1 degree (about 10 km)** grid.

How to read: use the time control to step through the months; emissions rise in the growing season after fertiliser and manure application. Lower the opacity slider to see place names underneath. Open Data Values and click the map for the value in a cell.

Carbon monoxide emission flux in kg per m² per second: a mass emitted, not a concentration. **Monthly, August 2025**, **global** at **0.5 by 0.625 degrees (about 50 km)**. From the NASA MERRA-2 reanalysis, which builds emissions from inventories and satellite fire data.

How to read: industrial regions show in every month; in August 2025 the fires in north-west Iberia, Canada and southern Africa stand out as well. The month is fixed; there is no time control.

Ammonia (NH3) concentration at ground level in µg/m³. **Latest hourly forecast step** of the CAMS European air quality ensemble, **Europe** on a **10 km** grid.

How to read: most ammonia comes from agriculture, so high values follow livestock regions and the farming calendar. This is a live forecast, so the map changes from hour to hour.

Carbon monoxide (CO) concentration at ground level in µg/m³. **Latest hourly forecast step** of the CAMS European air quality ensemble, **Europe** on a **10 km** grid.

How to read: CO marks incomplete combustion, such as domestic wood and coal heating and traffic. This is a live forecast, so the map changes from hour to hour.

Tropospheric NO2 column in molecules/cm² for **one day, 17 August 2025**, during the north-west Iberia fires. **Global**, TROPOMI pixels **5.5 by 3.5 km**; the record starts in May 2018.

How to read: one day of measurements, shaped by that day's weather; gaps are cloud. Look at north-west Spain for the fire signal. For the long-term pattern use the 2025 annual mean.

Total SO2 column in Dobson units for **one day, 17 August 2025**. **Global**, TROPOMI pixels **5.5 by 3.5 km**; the record starts in May 2018.

How to read: most of the map is background noise. Only the strongest sources stand out: large smelters, power plants, refineries and volcanoes.

Fine particles (PM2.5) at ground level in µg/m³. **Latest hourly forecast step** of the CAMS European air quality ensemble, **Europe** on a **10 km** grid.

How to read: use it to compare regions and follow pollution episodes. The EU annual limit value falls to 10 µg/m³ in 2030; official compliance is assessed at monitoring stations, not from this map. This is a live forecast, so the map changes from hour to hour.

Coarse particles (PM10) at ground level in µg/m³. **Latest hourly forecast step** of the CAMS European air quality ensemble, **Europe** on a **10 km** grid.

How to read: PM10 includes road wear, construction, farming and desert dust as well as combustion particles. Compare with the dust layer to separate Saharan dust from local sources. This is a live forecast, so the map changes from hour to hour.

Nitrogen dioxide (NO2) at ground level in µg/m³. **Latest hourly forecast step** of the CAMS European air quality ensemble, **Europe** on a **10 km** grid.

How to read: highest around cities, traffic corridors and shipping lanes. A 10 km grid shows the regional pattern, not the roadside peaks. This is a live forecast, so the map changes from hour to hour.

Ozone (O3) at ground level in µg/m³. **Latest hourly forecast step** of the CAMS European air quality ensemble, **Europe** on a **10 km** grid.

How to read: ozone forms in sunlight from NOx and VOCs, so it peaks downwind of cities and during heatwaves. This is a live forecast, so the map changes from hour to hour.

Sulphur dioxide (SO2) at ground level in µg/m³. **Latest hourly forecast step** of the CAMS European air quality ensemble, **Europe** on a **10 km** grid.

How to read: concentrations are low across most of Europe; the remaining hotspots sit around large plants, refineries and ports. This is a live forecast, so the map changes from hour to hour.

Dust aerosol optical depth at 550 nm, a dimensionless measure of how much dust dims sunlight through the whole air column. **Latest 3-hourly step** of the CAMS global forecast, **global** at about **40 km**.

How to read: Saharan dust events show as plumes moving north over the Mediterranean. Pair it with PM10 to see what reaches the ground. This is a live forecast, so the map changes from one forecast step to the next.

Total aerosol optical depth at 550 nm (dimensionless) from MODIS on Terra and Aqua, for **one day, 17 August 2025**, during the north-west Iberia fires. **Global**, about **10 km**.

How to read: high values mark smoke, dust or haze; gaps are cloud. On this day smoke from the Iberian fires spreads north along the Atlantic coast of France. Switch on the burnt area and Meteosat fire layers to see where it comes from.

Monthly mean aerosol optical depth at 550 nm (dimensionless) from the NASA MERRA-2 reanalysis, which combines a model with satellite observations. **August 2025**, **global** at about **50 km**; the record starts in 1980.

How to read: a gap-free monthly picture for comparing regions. Saharan dust dominates the south of the map. The month is fixed; there is no time control.

UV aerosol index for smoke lofted high by wildfire storm clouds (pyrocumulonimbus), dimensionless, from OMPS on Suomi NPP. **One day, 17 August 2025**, **global** at about **50 km**.

How to read: high values only appear after very large fires. On this day smoke from the north-west Iberia fires shows as a faint arc over Spain and France; compare it with the MODIS aerosol layer.

Active fires detected by Meteosat SEVIRI. **Live, latest scan, every 15 minutes**, over **Europe and Africa**; pixels are about 3 km below the satellite and 4 to 5 km over Europe.

How to read: only large, hot fires show. Zoom in on a region to see single detections.

Burnt areas of 30 ha or more in the **2025 fire season**, in **north-west Spain and northern Portugal**, mapped from MODIS and Sentinel-2 by Copernicus EFFIS.

How to read: the layer appears from zoom level 6; use the zoom button in this panel to fly there. Pair it with the Meteosat fire layer for when the land burned and with the aerosol layers for where the smoke went.

sources.name: Meteosat active fire, 11 to 18 August 2025, north-west Iberia

meta.description:
Pixels flagged as fire (red) or potential fire (amber) in at least one of 96 two-hourly Meteosat SEVIRI images, **11 to 18 August 2025**, over **north-west Iberia**, pixels about **4 by 5 km**.

How to read: one map for the whole week, showing the full extent of the episode. It appears from zoom level 6; use the zoom button in this panel to fly there.

Ground-level NO2 in ppb, **three-year mean, 1996 to 1998**, **global** at about **10 km**. Derived by NASA SEDAC from GOME, SCIAMACHY and GOME-2 satellite columns with a chemical transport model.

How to read: use it to compare regions. The 2010 to 2012 layer uses the same method and scale, and the comparison layer puts the two side by side.

Ground-level NO2 in ppb, **three-year mean, 2010 to 2012**, **global** at about **10 km**. Derived by NASA SEDAC from GOME, SCIAMACHY and GOME-2 satellite columns with a chemical transport model.

How to read: use it to compare regions. The 1996 to 1998 layer uses the same method and scale, and the comparison layer puts the two side by side.

Ground-level NO2 in ppb, **1996 to 1998 on one side and 2010 to 2012 on the other**, **global** at about **10 km**, from NASA SEDAC.

How to read: drag the divider across the map. Both periods use the same method and colour scale, so the change between them is directly comparable. Over western Europe concentrations fell; over parts of China and India they rose.

Tropospheric NO2 column in molecules/cm² from OMI on Aura, for **one day, 17 August 2025**. **Global**, pixels **13 by 24 km** below the satellite; the record starts in **October 2004**.

How to read: dark stripes are data gaps from cloud and from the instrument. OMI's value is its record since 2004; Sentinel-5P adds finer detail.

Surface NO2 in µg/m³ derived from Sentinel-5P columns with a chemistry transport model (ESA CitySatAir project). **694 midday overpasses, May 2018 to November 2022**, over **Oslo** in cells of about **6 by 8 km**.

How to read: each map is one overpass, not a daily or annual mean. Use the time control to step between overpasses. Click a cell and open Data Values for NO2, its uncertainty and the overpass time. The colour scale tops out at 40 µg/m³, the current EU annual limit value.

Surface NO2 in µg/m³ downscaled from the satellite product with models and local data (ESA CitySatAir project), showing NO2 at neighbourhood scale. **694 midday overpasses, May 2018 to November 2022**, over **Oslo** in **1 km** cells.

How to read: each map is one overpass, not a daily or annual mean. Use the time control to step between overpasses. Click a cell and open Data Values for NO2, its uncertainty and the overpass time. The colour scale tops out at 40 µg/m³, the current EU annual limit value.

Surface NO2 in µg/m³ derived from Sentinel-5P columns with a chemistry transport model (ESA CitySatAir project). **984 midday overpasses, May 2018 to December 2022**, over **Warsaw** in cells of about **6 by 8 km**.

How to read: each map is one overpass, not a daily or annual mean. Use the time control to step between overpasses. Click a cell and open Data Values for NO2, its uncertainty and the overpass time. The colour scale tops out at 40 µg/m³, the current EU annual limit value.

Surface NO2 in µg/m³ downscaled from the satellite product with the EPISODE dispersion model (ESA CitySatAir project), showing NO2 at neighbourhood scale. **984 midday overpasses, May 2018 to December 2022**, over **Warsaw** in **500 m** cells.

How to read: each map is one overpass, not a daily or annual mean. Use the time control to step between overpasses. Click a cell and open Data Values for NO2, its uncertainty and the overpass time. The colour scale tops out at 40 µg/m³, the current EU annual limit value.

Number of people per grid cell over **Europe**, on a **30 arc-second grid (about 1 km)**, modelled by WorldPop from census data and built-up area.

How to read: where people live. Switch on a pollutant layer as well to see who is exposed. Open Data Values and click the map for the value in a cell.

Air pollution health risk index for **every local administrative unit in EU28+**, **October 2025**, from the ESA AlpAirEO project, combining modelled pollution with population.

How to read: higher values mark units where pollution and population combine into a higher health risk. Click a unit and open Data Values for the index by cause of death (all causes, cardiovascular, respiratory) and the pollutant that dominates each.

stories.title: From continent to chimney
stories.description: Seven steps from the global CO2 field down to a single steelworks and the people living next to it.

content.title: CO2 over the whole planet
content.description: This is the CO2 in the atmosphere today, from the [Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service](https://atmosphere.copernicus.eu/ghg-services) global forecast. The background is about 420 ppm everywhere, and human emissions add only a few ppm on top. To separate that small signal from the large background, Europe is building [CO2MVS](https://knowledge4policy.ec.europa.eu/node/44439/), a capacity to monitor anthropogenic CO2 that combines models like this one with dedicated satellites. Its satellite part is the Copernicus [CO2M](https://www.eoportal.org/satellite-missions/co2m) constellation, which will measure CO2 over a wide swath, with an NO2 instrument to pick out plumes from combustion.

content.title: Methane that stays
content.description: A full year of [Sentinel-5P](https://sentiwiki.copernicus.eu/web/s5p-mission) methane retrievals, averaged to remove noise. Persistent enhancements stand out over coal basins, oil and gas regions and wetlands. Methane has a short atmospheric lifetime, so cuts show up quickly. That is the basis of the [Global Methane Pledge](https://www.globalmethanepledge.org/) and of the EU [Methane Regulation](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1787/oj) for the energy sector. The lines are gas and oil pipelines from [Global Energy Monitor](https://globalenergymonitor.org/projects/global-gas-infrastructure-tracker/).

content.title: Where fuel is burned
content.description: NO2 comes out of the same combustion as CO2 but lasts only a few hours, so it stays close to its source. The 2025 annual mean from Sentinel-5P, processed by [S5P-PAL](https://maps.s5p-pal.com/), traces power plants, industry, cities and shipping lanes across Europe.

content.title: Rhine-Ruhr: emitters and what is burning
content.description: The densest industrial cluster in Germany. Purple dots are NOx emissions estimated from Sentinel-5P NO2 and ERA5 winds, from the catalogue of the [Max Planck Institute for Chemistry](https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-15-3051-2023) distributed by ESA's [World Emission](https://www.world-emission.com/) service. The small markers are coal, gas, oil and waste plants from the [Global Power Plant Database](https://datasets.wri.org/dataset/globalpowerplantdatabase). Most satellite-detected sources match a power plant. The rest are cement plants, smelters, industrial areas and cities.

content.title: Shipping lanes, counted ship by ship
content.description: Ship NOx emissions in 2023 from the STEAM model of the Finnish Meteorological Institute, computed for each ship from its AIS positions, engine data and the weather, for the ESA [EO4SEM](https://eo4sem.apex.esa.int/) project. This is a bottom-up inventory. The North Sea and the Baltic are NOx Emission Control Areas under [MARPOL Annex VI](https://www.imo.org/en/OurWork/Environment/Pages/Special-Areas-Marpol.aspx), with tighter limits for ships built since 2021.

content.title: One steelworks: Taranto
content.description: The Acciaierie d'Italia plant in Taranto, Puglia, is one of the largest steelworks in Europe. Each shape is one CO2 plume detected by hyperspectral satellites ([EnMAP](https://www.enmap.org/), [PRISMA](https://www.asi.it/en/earth-science/prisma/), [EMIT](https://earth.jpl.nasa.gov/emit/) and [Tanager](https://carbonmapper.org/)) at 30 to 60 m and quantified by the ESA [ICO2NS](https://browser.apex.esa.int/external/eoresults.esa.int/stac/collections/ico2ns_co2_plumes?.language=en) project. There are six detections between April 2025 and April 2026. The NOx catalogue also lists a source here, with no power plant matched. Facility-level checks like these can support verification of emissions reported under the [EU ETS](https://climate.ec.europa.eu/eu-action/eu-emissions-trading-system-eu-ets_en).

content.title: Who lives next to it
content.description: The plant borders the city of Taranto, home to close to 190,000 people, and its Tamburi district. Population from [WorldPop](https://www.worldpop.org/) shows where people live around the site. An emission becomes a health question once it reaches the people who breathe it, which is what the EU [Ambient Air Quality Directive](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2024/2881/oj) is about.

stories.title: Counting emissions two ways
stories.description: Inventories count emissions from statistics; satellites infer them from the air. Six steps from the satellite view and a bottom-up inventory to checks on single plants.

content.title: What the air shows
content.description: NO2 from the Copernicus [Sentinel-5P](https://sentiwiki.copernicus.eu/web/s5p-mission) satellite, averaged over 2025 by [S5P-PAL](https://maps.s5p-pal.com/). NO2 comes from burning fuel and lasts only a few hours, so the map shows where emissions happen: power plants, industry, cities and shipping lanes. Emissions can be counted from statistics or inferred from measurements like these, and the [IPCC 2019 Refinement](https://www.ipcc-nggip.iges.or.jp/public/2019rf/) describes comparing the two as a way to verify inventories.

content.title: Emissions from statistics
content.description: Inventories estimate emissions from activity data multiplied by emission factors. For shipping, the STEAM model of the Finnish Meteorological Institute does this ship by ship, from AIS positions, engine data and the weather, for the ESA [EO4SEM](https://eo4sem.apex.esa.int/) project. This is ship NOx in 2023 over the Mediterranean, in kg per grid cell per year. The main routes and the ports stand out.

content.title: Emissions inferred from the air
content.description: Each dot is a NOx emission rate estimated from Sentinel-5P NO2 and ERA5 winds by the flux divergence method. The [catalogue](https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-15-3051-2023) lists 1,139 sources worldwide, and its estimates agree with those reported by the German Environment Agency (UBA) and the US EPA within 20 % on average. Air pollutant emissions are reported under the [NEC Directive](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2016/2284/oj) and the UNECE Air Convention.

content.title: Matching a point to a plant: Bełchatów
content.description: Bełchatów in central Poland is the largest lignite power station in Europe. The satellite NOx estimate sits on the plant listed in the Global Power Plant Database: 0.50 kg/s, with an error of 0.08 kg/s, for 2021. Linking a top-down estimate to a named installation is what makes it comparable with reported figures, such as those in the EEA [Industrial Emissions Portal](https://industry.eea.europa.eu/).

content.title: Agriculture: NOx from cropland
content.description: Fertilised and manured fields also release NOx. KNMI's [DECSO](https://www.temis.nl/emissions/region_europe/archive_annual_data.php) algorithm estimates emissions from Sentinel-5P NO2 by inverse modelling. This is its cropland share for July 2025, in kg of nitrogen per hectare per year on a 10 km grid. Emissions peak in the growing season. Agricultural air pollutant emissions fall under the [NEC Directive](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2016/2284/oj), where ammonia is the main agricultural commitment.

content.title: Steel imports: Ereğli
content.description: The Erdemir plant in Ereğli, on the Black Sea coast, is one of the largest steelworks in Türkiye. The ESA ICO2NS project detected three CO2 plumes here with EnMAP in 2025 and 2026. Iron and steel are covered by the EU [Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism](https://taxation-customs.ec.europa.eu/carbon-border-adjustment-mechanism_en), which prices the emissions embedded in imports. Independent facility-level estimates are one way to check emissions reported by producers outside the EU.

stories.title: The air Europe breathes
stories.description: Five steps on air quality in Europe: today's particles, the Po Valley, Oslo and Warsaw street by street, and who is most exposed.

content.title: Fine particles today
content.description: Fine particles are the air pollutant most closely tied to premature death. The revised [Ambient Air Quality Directive (EU) 2024/2881](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2024/2881/oj) lowers the annual PM2.5 limit value to 10 µg/m³ from 2030, closer to the [WHO 2021 guideline](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789240034228) of 5 µg/m³. This is today's CAMS European forecast at about 10 km, updated every hour.

content.title: The Po Valley
content.description: Surface NO2 over the Po Valley, one of the most polluted basins in Europe: traffic, industry and farming, enclosed by the Alps, which trap air in winter. The annual NO2 limit value falls to 20 µg/m³ in 2030. A 10 km model smooths out the roadside peaks where most exceedances occur, so compliance is assessed at monitoring stations ([EEA overview](https://www.eea.europa.eu/en/topics/in-depth/air-pollution)).

content.title: From satellite to street: Oslo
content.description: The ESA [CitySatAir](https://citysatair.nilu.no/) project (KNMI, NILU, Lobelia) turned Sentinel-5P columns into surface NO2 in µg/m³ and downscaled it to 1 km over Oslo. This overpass on 27 October 2021 separates the port, the main roads and the residential areas, which a single satellite pixel averages into one value. The detail comes from combining the satellite data with models and local measurements.

content.title: Heating and traffic: Warsaw
content.description: The same [CitySatAir](https://citysatair.nilu.no/) method over Warsaw, here at 500 m, for the midday overpass on 15 January 2020. Across most of the city surface NO2 was between 7 and 27 µg/m³, higher along the main roads. The two bands of highest values, up to about 69 µg/m³, sit on the Żerań and Siekierki coal-fired heat and power plants, shown as dots from the [Global Power Plant Database](https://datasets.wri.org/dataset/globalpowerplantdatabase). The fine pattern comes from combining the satellite data with a dispersion model, so it shows where NO2 is likely to be highest rather than a measurement in each street.

content.title: Who is most exposed
content.description: Pollution becomes a health question when it meets people. The ESA [AlpAirEO](https://eo4society.esa.int/projects/alpaireo/) project, led by DLR, combined modelled pollution with population into a risk index for every local administrative unit in the EU. Milan and the Lombardy plain have the highest values in Europe. Click a unit to see which pollutant drives the risk for all-cause, cardiovascular and respiratory mortality.
